rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to maximize the chance of observing all 10 compounds and reveal crowded retention regions. The moderate gradient duration and midpoint temperature leave room to optimize selectivity and run time in subsequent injections.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin can be traded for speed. Keep temperature and endpoints fixed to isolate the effect of gradient steepness.

Keep the fast gradient and raise temperature to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity separates the crowded middle peaks. This targets better resolution while retaining the zero time penalty achieved in injection 2.

Slightly lengthen the gradient at the best temperature to improve the remaining under-resolved pair while checking for selectivity shifts in the middle cluster. The last peak should remain near the zero-time-penalty region.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; test a slightly shallower gradient to explore nearby methods with comparable performance. Lowering the endpoint may improve the marginal separations while keeping the last peak close to the zero-time-penalty region.

Test a small temperature increase to improve the marginal middle-cluster separation and shorten retention. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this explores whether a nearby method can retain that score with a larger resolution margin.

Return to the successful 55 C temperature and test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention while changing gradient selectivity. This explores another potential maximum-score method without repeating previous conditions.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness from injection 7 to improve the under-resolved pair, targeting full resolution while keeping the last peak below 8 minutes. The other marginal pair has some resolution margin to accommodate this change.

Further flatten the gradient slightly to lift the remaining R = 1.47 pair above 1.5. Extrapolation from injections 7 and 8 places the last peak near 8 minutes, potentially preserving zero time penalty and reaching another maximum-score method.

Test a higher starting organic fraction combined with a shallower gradient to seek more resolution margin while keeping the last peak near 8 minutes. The maximum score is already secured; this explores an alternative maximum-score method.

Test the low-temperature selectivity regime with the fast gradient, since cooling may separate the middle peaks through a different elution order. This explores a distinct route to full resolution with little or no time penalty, while retaining the established maximum-score method.

Test intermediate-temperature selectivity on the fast gradient to map the transition between the 40 C and 55 C peak patterns. This may identify a faster fully resolved method; the previously achieved CRF of 1.000 remains the campaign maximum.

Test a faster gradient at higher temperature and starting organic fraction to explore separation beyond the middle-pair elution-order crossover. This is an exploratory search for a shorter maximum-score method, with the established CRF 1.000 methods retained.

Increase starting organic fraction to probe selectivity on the reversed-order side of the remaining close pair, while lengthening the gradient to preserve surrounding separations. This tests a potentially faster alternative to the established maximum-score methods.

Continue increasing the starting organic fraction with a compensating longer gradient to improve the remaining close pair on this selectivity branch. Monitor the early peaks for compression while seeking full resolution within the zero-time-penalty window.

Preserve injection 4’s successful gradient slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute while ending the ramp earlier. Since all peaks previously eluted before this new ramp ends, this method should reproduce the maximum CRF of 1.000 with a lower final organic fraction.

Keep the proven gradient slope while lowering the endpoint further and ending the ramp at 8 minutes. All peaks should still elute during the unchanged portion of the gradient, preserving the maximum CRF of 1.000.

Test a gradient slope between those of injections 8 and 9, targeting both marginal pairs above 1.5 with the last peak below 8 minutes. This may preserve the maximum CRF with a slightly better resolution margin than injection 4.

Retain the proven gradient slope but begin the final hold earlier, after the first nine peaks have eluted. This tests whether the last compound still elutes before 8 minutes, potentially preserving maximum CRF with a lower organic endpoint.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 9 to improve its closer early-middle pair while monitoring the other marginal separation. The last peak is expected near 8.2 minutes, within the zero-time-penalty region demonstrated by injection 19.

Lengthen injection 10’s gradient to improve its R = 1.10 pair while retaining the stronger separation of the other middle pair. This tests whether a higher-starting-organic method can reach full resolution before the time penalty begins.

Slightly flatten injection 21’s gradient to raise the remaining R = 1.41 pair above 1.5 while preserving the other middle pair’s resolution margin. The last peak is expected near 9 minutes, testing another potential maximum-score method at the edge of the zero-time-penalty region.

Preserve injection 9’s gradient slope while lowering the final organic fraction to 0.60. Since the outlet ramp ends at 8.65 minutes, after the previously observed last peak, this should retain its maximum CRF and minimum resolution of 1.58.

Use injection 8’s gradient slope but end the ramp early, testing whether the final hold changes the marginal separation enough to achieve full resolution. The established maximum-score methods remain available regardless of this exploratory result.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 20, targeting full resolution with the last peak around 8.3 minutes and no time penalty. This tests a lower-endpoint alternative expected to match the already-achieved maximum CRF of 1.000.
